h1: Building a Context-Aware, Compliant LLM Agent for High-Volume Support Deflection
h6: Building a Context-Aware, Compliant LLM Agent for High-Volume Support Deflection
p: Engineered a stateful conversational AI agent trained strictly on proprietary banking databases to autonomously resolve Tier-1 helpdesk tickets without regulatory breaches.

CoreTech Systems, a rapidly scaling digital banking platform, experienced an exponential surge in Tier-1 customer support requests regarding account configurations, balance discrepancies, and basic transaction disputes. Their human engineering and customer success queues were severely backed up, causing standard ticket resolution times to spiral past 36 hours. Legacy rule-based chatbots failed completely at comprehending conversational nuances, frustrating premium users and driving up customer churn rates. However, because they operate in FinTech, implementing an off-the-shelf LLM was a massive regulatory risk; a single "hallucinated" piece of financial advice could trigger severe legal penalties.

We engineered a highly restrictive, stateful conversational AI agent utilizing a localized Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture. Instead of relying on a foundational model's pre-trained knowledge, the agent is strictly tethered to CoreTech's proprietary product databases, security boundary documentation, and historical Zendesk transaction paths. The agent operates inside a custom validation framework that monitors semantic inputs in real-time. We utilized deterministic function calling to allow the model to pull live transaction data securely via secure API endpoints. The guardrails are absolute: if a user query falls outside the vectorized documentation or requires account mutation (like transferring funds), the system immediately halts generation and forwards the complex edge case to human personnel, pre-compiling the entire historical memory context so the human agent loses zero time.

"We were terrified of customer-facing AI hallucinations that could land us in regulatory hot water or expose financial data. Stackgrid didn't just build a chatbot; they built a deterministic infrastructure. This architecture doesn't guess—it functions exactly within the mathematical guardrails defined, solving user problems instantly while keeping our legal and compliance teams entirely comfortable."

h1: Replacing Legacy ERP Invoicing Bottlenecks with an Autonomous Middleware Pipeline
h6: Replacing Legacy ERP Invoicing Bottlenecks with an Autonomous Middleware Pipeline
p: Bypassed manual invoicing friction for a global supply chain firm by deploying an event-driven middleware orchestration layer that cuts processing time from 48 hours to 11 minutes.

Simplify Digital Co. was processing upwards of 4,000 multi-currency, cross-border customs invoices every single week. Their legacy Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) platform lacked native intelligent automation, requiring five full-time operational data clerks to manually extract lines of nested line-item data, verify raw totals against corresponding digital purchase orders, and flag currency variances. This manual entry bottleneck delayed logistics routing by up to 48 hours per batch. Crucially, human transcription typos frequently triggered compliance discrepancies at customs checkpoints, resulting in steep operational fines and supply-chain logjams that choked their weekly throughput.

We designed and engineered a custom, event-driven middleware orchestration layer that connects directly to Simplify Digital Co.’s internal email servers and secure file transfer protocols via private webhooks. When a raw invoice payload lands, it triggers a multi-modal data pipeline that strips out metadata and flattens nested tabular document arrays.

The ingestion engine streams the data blocks through an isolated instance of Claued 3.5 Sonnex to convert unstructured text into explicit, schema-validated JSON arrays. To ensure total operational stability, the pipeline processes data through a strict deterministic verification layer. This layer dynamically queries the company's central SQL ledger, cross-checks unit prices against historical contracts, runs tax calculations, and logs the execution metrics. If the values align within a strict 0.01% error margin, the system automatically executes a state mutation in the client's live accounting database, completing the transaction ledger instantly without a human ever touching a keyboard.

"Our manual data entry pipelines were completely strangling our margins and causing massive shipping delays at international customs checkpoints. Stackgrid bypassed the standard AI market fluff and engineered a robust, infrastructure-level solution. The autonomous pipeline completely transformed our unit economics, slashed our processing timelines from days to minutes, and allowed our business to scale throughput without forcing us to scale our human operational headcount."

h1: Deploying Predictive AI to Automate Customer Success and Eradicate Churn
h6: Deploying Predictive AI to Automate Customer Success and Eradicate Churn
p: Engineered a predictive AI middleware pipeline that analyzes real-time product telemetry to autonomously trigger personalized onboarding interventions, drastically reducing enterprise user churn.

Velosite SaaS was acquiring enterprise users rapidly, but their Customer Success team was drowning in reactive support operations. Because they lacked real-time, unified visibility into product usage telemetry, they could not identify which high-value clients were at risk of churning until it was too late. Manual "health-check" routines were painfully inefficient, requiring CS reps to dig through siloed Mixpanel dashboards, while generic, static email drip campaigns were being completely ignored by frustrated accounts. The manual latency between a user experiencing platform friction and a CS rep reaching out was costing the company significant recurring revenue.

We deployed an intelligent, event-driven retention architecture that bridges the gap between raw data and customer communication. The system ingests raw product usage telemetry (clicks, feature adoption rates, session durations) directly via secure webhooks into a centralized vector environment.

A custom pipeline continuously analyzes this behavioral data against historical churn patterns. When the system detects a "drop-off signature"—for instance, a user failing to configure a core integration within 48 hours of account creation—it autonomously triggers a hyper-personalized intervention. The middleware queries an LLM to generate a highly specific, context-aware message offering an exact solution to the user's friction point. Simultaneously, it pushes a fully compiled diagnostic brief into the Customer Success team's internal Slack channel, ensuring human reps only step in when high-touch intervention is mathematically necessary.

"Before this deployment, our CS team was constantly putting out fires and reacting to churn after the fact. Stackgrid didn't just build a basic integration; they built an intelligent infrastructure that actually predicts user friction in real-time. It completely automated our health scoring and allowed our team to focus purely on high-level strategy instead of manual data digging. Our retention metrics transformed entirely."

Illegal Activity: Anything violating French, European Union, or other applicable law, including fraud, unlicensed distribution of regulated goods, distribution of illegal material, or evasion of sanctions.

Bulk Unsolicited Messaging: You may not use Axiom's mail or messaging connectors to send unsolicited bulk communications, or to circumvent the sending limits of the services you have connected.
Scraping in Violation of Terms: You may not configure Axiom to extract data from platforms in breach of those platforms' terms of service or robots.txt directives.
Circumventing Approval Gates: Axiom stops and asks before actions that send, delete, publish, or spend. You may not attempt to disable, automate around, or otherwise defeat that gate.

Infrastructure Load: You may not deliberately generate artificial task volume intended to degrade the service, exhaust rate limits, or inflate compute costs.

Reverse Engineering: You may not decompile, disassemble, or reverse-engineer the Axiom application to extract credentials, replicate its architecture, or build a competing product. Note that until an API proxy is in place, the beta build contains service credentials; extracting and using them is a violation of this policy and of the underlying providers' terms.

Security Testing: You may not run penetration tests, red-teaming scripts, or stress tests against Axiom's infrastructure without written authorisation. If you find a vulnerability, report it — see below.

Google (Gemini API and Google Workspace services)
Any service you connect, including Notion, Slack, and others

Report: Refer conduct to law enforcement or the affected third-party provider where the law requires it or the conduct warrants it.
We monitor aggregate usage patterns and error rates to keep the service running. We do not read the content of your tasks — see the Privacy Policy for what that means precisely.

p: Axiom ("we," "our," or "us") is committed to being precise about what leaves your machine and who processes it. This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, disclose, and safeguard your information when you visit useaxiom.com and when you use the Axiom macOS application.
Axiom is currently in beta. This policy will change as the product changes, and the date below will change with it.
We collect information in a few distinct categories. They are not treated the same way.
Account Data: Your email address and authentication credentials, provided when you create an account. Stored with Supabase on servers located in the European Union.

Usage Data: The number of interactions you run each month, your subscription tier, and the timestamps of those runs. This exists to enforce plan limits and to tell us whether the product works. It is stored separately from the content of what you asked for.

Task Content: The instruction you give Axiom, together with whatever context is required to carry it out. Depending on the task, this may include calendar entries, email content, file contents, or messages from the apps you have connected. See "AI Processing" below, which is the section that matters most.

Connected Application Data: When you authorise a third-party service such as Google Calendar, Gmail, Google Drive, Notion, or Slack, Axiom accesses only what is needed to complete the tasks you ask for. Authorisation is handled through Composio. We never receive or store your passwords for those services.

Your Own Model Key (Operator tier): If you supply your own API key, it is encrypted on your Mac using the macOS safeStorage API and stored locally on that machine. It is never transmitted to our servers and never written to our database.
Derivative Data: Standard server logs generated when you access the website, including IP address, browser type, operating system, and pages viewed. We run no advertising or profiling trackers.
This is the section to read carefully.

Axiom does not run a local model. To execute your tasks, task content is transmitted to third-party AI providers — currently Google (Gemini). The content of your instruction, and the application data required to fulfil it, leaves your machine and is processed on Google's infrastructure under Google's terms.
No Training: Your task content is not used to train, fine-tune, or improve any model, ours or anyone else's.
No Sale: We do not sell, trade, or rent your task content or any other data described in this policy.
No Access: We do not read your task content, except where you explicitly send us something in the course of a support request.
If you handle material you are not permitted to transmit to a third-party AI provider, do not put it through Axiom.
Operating Axiom requires a small number of third-party providers. Each is listed below with its purpose and location.
Supabase — account data and usage records — European Union (Frankfurt)
Google (Gemini API) — AI task execution — United States
Composio — third-party application connections — United States
Vercel — website hosting — United States and global CDN
Transfers to providers outside the European Economic Area rely on those providers' Standard Contractual Clauses. This list will grow as the product does, and this page will be updated when it does.
To execute the tasks you explicitly ask for (contractual necessity)
To keep the service running and diagnose failures (legitimate interest)
To contact you about the beta and about material changes to the service (legitimate interest)To operate your account and enforce the limits of your plan (contractual necessity)
To operate your account and enforce the limits of your plan (contractual necessity)
Account and Usage Data: Retained while your account is active, and for thirty days after you delete it.

Task Content: Not retained by us beyond what is required to complete the task and display it in your task history. Deleting a task removes it. Retention by third-party AI providers is governed by their own terms, not ours.

We use administrative, technical, and physical security measures to help protect your personal and corporate data. While we have taken reasonable steps to secure the personal information you provide to us, please be aware that despite our efforts, no security measures are perfect or impenetrable, and no method of data transmission can be guaranteed against any interception or other type of misuse. Our internal databases utilize AES-256 encryption.
Account data sits behind Supabase row-level security policies. Locally stored credentials are encrypted using the macOS safeStorage API. All traffic is encrypted in transit.

We will also be direct about the limits: Axiom is beta software built by one person and has not undergone an independent security audit. No security measure is perfect, and no method of transmission over the internet can be guaranteed against interception. If and when an audit happens, this page will say so.
Axiom is not intended for anyone under the age of sixteen, and we do not knowingly collect information from anyone under sixteen. If we learn that we have, we will delete it.
The website uses only the cookies necessary to operate it. We do not use advertising cookies, web beacons, or third-party tracking pixels.
If you have questions about this Privacy Policy, wish to exercise your rights, or need to raise anything else regarding how your data is handled, contact supportAxiom26@gmail.com
